title: "5. More Experiments, Easier Targets"

## **Why Multivariate Normal Distributions?**

[Explain why controlled distributions are useful.]

## **The Experimental Strategy**

We systematically vary:

- dimensionality,
- variance structure,
- correlation structure,
- anisotropy,
- coordinate representation.

The main quantities of interest are:

- warmup length,
- nested $\widehat{R}$,
- mean squared error.

### Highlight Plots

<div class="button-row">

  <img id="d100-plot" src="../figures/chapter05/d100/highlight_noTransform.png" alt="100-dimensional MVN highlight plot">

  noTransform:   '../figures/chapter05/d100/highlight_noTransform.png',
  withTransform: '../figures/chapter05/d100/highlight_withTransform.png'
};

document.querySelectorAll('.d100-btn').forEach(btn => {
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    document.getElementById('d100-plot').src = d100Files[btn.dataset.image];

    document.querySelectorAll('.d100-btn').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
    btn.classList.add('active');
  });
});

## **What Are We Looking For?**

We are looking for the connection between the MSE vs. $\widehat{R}_{\nu}$ on different distributions.
